finding.description: The file points attackers to the sensitive paths.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: robots-discloses-paths (The file points attackers to the sensitive paths. Evidence: Disallow: /admin, /backup/, /.env, /export/). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Recommended fix: Remove the sensitive Disallow entries ( /admin, /backup/, /.env, /export/ ) from robots.txt and do not use robots.txt to hide or protect them. Enforce server-side authentication and authorization on those paths instead, and use proper access controls / noindex for any sensitive content that must not be crawled or accessed publicly.

fix.summary: Serve the normal catalogue page at /robots.txt so no sensitive Disallow entries are disclosed.
fix.risk: Legitimate crawlers receive HTML instead of robots directives and may crawl all paths.

applied.find:
if (path === '/robots.txt') return [200, { 'content-type': 'text/plain' }, 'User-agent: *
Disallow: /admin
Disallow: /backup/
Disallow: /.env
Disallow: /export/
']; // FLAW 10: robots.txt advertises the sensitive paths
applied.replace:
if (path === '/robots.txt') return html(page('index.html').replace('', PRODUCTS.map((p) => `

${p.name}

${p.price} €

`).join('')));
